top_documented.title: Improved Approximation and Tight Competition for Simple Auctions
top_documented.abstract: We study simple auctions for one additive buyer whose values for $m$ items are independent. Write $\mathrm{REV}$ for optimal revenue, $\mathrm{SREV}$ and $\mathrm{BREV}$ for the revenues from separate selling and grand bundling, and $\mathrm{BSPA}_2$ for grand-bundle second-price revenue with two independent bidders. For independent regular items, we prove $\mathrm{REV}\le\mathrm{BSPA}_2\le2\mathrm{BREV}$. This establishes tight approximation and competition guarantees for bundling under regularity and answers an open question from Beyhaghi et al. (EC 2025). For general independent items, we prove $\mathrm{REV} \le \mathrm{SREV} + \frac{π^2}{6}\mathrm{BREV} \le 2.645 \max\{\mathrm{SREV}, \mathrm{BREV}\}$. top_documented.title: Slack and Budget Breaking in Threshold Team Production
top_documented.abstract: A threshold system completes a public task only after $κ$ verifiable shares are publicly committed. If the honest schedule creates \( \Nstar=κ+Δ\) share opportunities by deadline $t^\star$, then $Δ$ shares are slack such that a coalition delays completion if and only if it withholds at least $Δ+1$ shares. The incentive problem is therefore to price the cheapest sabotage set. Agents receive a direct fee $f$ per committed share. A delaying coalition may also obtain delay value at most $L$, and may earn additional fee revenue during recovery after the deadline. top_documented.title: The Hardness of Dominant Strategy Mechanism Design, Revisited
top_documented.abstract: We study the communication complexity of \emph{dominant-strategy incentive-compatible} (DSIC) mechanisms for combinatorial auctions. For $γ\in [\log m, m]$, let $\mathsf{DSIC_{GEN}}(m, γ)$, $\mathsf{DSIC_{XOS}}(m, γ)$, and $\mathsf{DSIC_{GS}}(m, γ)$ denote the best approximation ratio attainable by a deterministic, individually rational, no-negative-transfers, DSIC mechanism using at most $2^γ$ communication over $m$ items, for general monotone, XOS, and gross substitutes (GS) valuations, respectively. We give a unified proof that shows $\mathsf{DSIC_{GEN}}(m, γ) = Ω(m/γ)$, $\mathsf{DSIC_{XOS}}(m, γ) = Ω((m/γ)^{1/5})$, and $\mathsf{DSIC_{GS}}(m, γ) = Ω((m/γ)^{1/7})$. top_documented.title: Coarse Revenue Guarantee in First Price Auction and Beyond
top_documented.abstract: I study the coarse revenue guarantee (CRG) of the single-unit first-price auction with common values. The CRG is the minimum expected revenue over all information structures and all Bayes coarse correlated equilibria (BCCE), the equilibrium notion to which no-regret learning leads. Identical play, in which all bidders submit the same bid, attains the worst-case revenue, and this reduction yields a closed-form characterization. The coarse guarantee is positive and increases with the number of bidders $N$. It lies strictly below the revenue guarantee of Bergemann, Brooks and Morris (2017) at every finite $n$, and the gap between the two closes at rate $\log N / N$. top_documented.title: A Faster Auction Algorithm for Weighted Matroid Intersection
top_documented.abstract: We consider the weighted matroid intersection problem in the independence-oracle model. A sequence of works by Huang--Kakimura--Kamiyama~[SODA'16 \& Math. Program'19], Chekuri--Quanrud~[SODA'16], Quanrud~[ICALP'24], and Dudeja--Grilnberger~[IPCO'26] has developed efficient $(1-\varepsilon)$-approximation algorithms for this problem. We present a simple deterministic auction algorithm that, given two matroids on a common ground set of size $n$, computes a $(1-\varepsilon)$-approximate maximum-weight common independent set using $O(n \varepsilon^{-2} \log^2(n))$ independence-oracle queries. This is the first deterministic $(1-\varepsilon)$-approximation algorithm for the weighted matroid intersection problem whose query complexity is nearly linear in $n$ and polynomial in $1/\varepsilon$. top_documented.title: Improved Pass Complexity for Semi-Streaming Matching in General Graphs via Budgeted Price Approach
top_documented.abstract: We present a simple deterministic semi-streaming algorithm that computes a $(1-\varepsilon)$-approximate maximum matching in general graphs in $O(1/\varepsilon^{2})$ passes. This matches the pass complexity of the auction algorithm of Assadi, Liu, and Tarjan~[SOSA'21] for bipartite graphs, and answers Open Question~2 of Assadi~[SOSA'24 \& TheoretiCS'25]. Our approach, which we call the \emph{budgeted price approach}, is very different from the previous $\mathrm{poly}(1/\varepsilon)$-pass semi-streaming algorithms for $(1-\varepsilon)$-approximation of matching in general graphs and improves their pass complexity.
